movement_source: row 'Cost to income ratio', column Sep 24 (FY24) column -> column Sep 25 (FY25) column
headline: NAB's cash-basis cost-to-income ratio rose 0.8 ppt in FY25, from 46.5% in FY24 to 47.3% in FY25 (results book KPI table). The movement reflects negative jaws: operating income grew 2.9% (net operating income $20,813m vs $20,236m) while operating expenses grew 4.6% ($9,848m vs $9,413m), so expense growth outran income growth and pushed the ratio up. On the statutory basis the ratio rose 1.1 ppt (49.6% vs 48.5%). The bank does not publish a walk of the CTI ratio itself, so the income and expense contributions cannot be split into ppt; the drivers are presented with their growth rates and the expense-side decomposition.

drivers.columns: Sep 25 vs Sep 24 net operating income
drivers.narrative: Net operating income rose 2.9% to $20,813m (FY24: $20,236m), driven by volume growth and higher Markets & Treasury income, partially offset by higher customer-related remediation charges and business disposals/run-offs. Income growth of 2.9% was slower than expense growth, so it did not offset the expense-driven rise in the ratio.

Operating expenses rose 4.6% to $9,848m (FY24: $9,413m), outrunning income growth and raising the ratio. The bank's YoY expense walk decomposes the $435m increase: Salary related +$267m, Volume related +$143m, Technology & Investment +$213m, Depreciation & Amortisation +$42m, Productivity -$420m, Other +$131m, EU -$71m, Payroll review and remediation +$130m. Excluding payroll review and remediation, expenses rose 3.2%.

drivers.bank_label: Notable and restructuring items on either side
drivers.narrative: Within expenses, payroll review and remediation costs of $130m (FY25) and lower EU-related costs of -$71m are notable items. Excluding payroll review and remediation, expense growth was 3.2% rather than 4.6%. These items are embedded in the expense driver and are not separately quantified in ppt for the CTI ratio.

disagreements.explanation: The primary reporting basis is cash earnings; the statutory-basis CTI is a different measure reported as context.

limitations: The bank does not publish a walk/bridge of the cost-to-income ratio itself, so the income and expense contributions cannot be split into ppt. The drivers are presented with their growth rates and the expense-side decomposition; the ppt split is left unquantified.

The expense walk (investor presentation p25) is the bank's decomposition of the expense growth driver, not of the CTI ratio; its bars are in $m and are used to explain the expense driver, not as CTI ppt contributions.

The income growth of 2.9% is stated in the results book (p5); the investor presentation corroborates the FY25 net operating income via half-year figures (10,268 + 10,545 = 20,813) but does not publish the FY income growth rate directly.
Statutory-basis CTI rose 1.1 ppt (49.6% vs 48.5%), a different basis from the primary cash-basis movement of +0.8 ppt; reported as context.
The investor presentation does not publish the CTI ratio value or a CTI walk; the CTI movement is sourced from the results book KPI table only.
The submitted residual was malformed (non-numeric value), so no residual is stated.
